name: Variable
description: Variable: a letter that stands for a number that is unknown or can take different values.

name: Power
description: Power: a product of equal factors written in short form, so 1.05^3 means 1.05 · 1.05 · 1.05. The raised number is the exponent.

name: Ratio
description: Ratio: a comparison of two quantities by division, written a : b or as a fraction.

name: Equation and solution
description:
Equation: a statement that two expressions are equal.
Solution: a value of the variable that makes the statement true.

name: Solve a linear equation
description: solve a linear equation by doing the same to both sides, including equations with brackets and fractions

name: Justify the steps in solving an equation
description: explain what was done to both sides at each step, and check the answer by substituting it back

name: Set up an equation from a practical situation
description: choose what the variable stands for, write an equation that describes the situation, solve it, and state the answer in a sentence with units

name: Coordinate system
description: Coordinate system: two perpendicular number lines, the x-axis and the y-axis, where every point is given by a pair (x, y).

name: Draw the line for y = ax + b
description: make a table of values for an expression of the form y = ax + b and draw its line in a coordinate system

name: Solve an equation with a digital tool
description: solve an equation with CAS, or by finding where two graphs meet in GeoGebra, and write down what was done

name: System of equations
description: System of equations: two equations with two unknowns that must both be true at the same time. Its solution is a pair of values.

name: Solve a system of equations by substitution
description: solve a system of two linear equations by expressing one unknown from one equation and substituting it into the other

name: Solve a system of equations graphically
description: solve a system of two linear equations by drawing both lines and reading off where they cross, by hand or in GeoGebra

name: Inequality
description: Inequality: a statement that one expression is less than or greater than another, written with <, >, ≤ or ≥. Its solution is usually a whole range of values.

name: Solve a linear inequality
description: solve a linear inequality, turning the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, and state which values satisfy it

name: Compare strategies for solving equations
description: compare solving by hand, by graph and with CAS for a given problem, and argue which suits it best

name: Fractions and decimals
description:
Fraction: a number written as a numerator divided by a denominator.
Decimal: the same number written with a decimal point. Every fraction has a decimal form.

name: Percentage
description: Percentage: a number of hundredths, so 40 % means 40 out of 100, or 0.40.

name: Calculate a percentage of an amount
description: calculate a given percentage of an amount, such as 25 % of 480 kr

name: Calculate what percentage one amount is of another
description: calculate what percentage a part is of a whole

name: Percentage change
description: Percentage change: the change divided by the original value, written as a percentage.

name: Calculate a percentage change
description: calculate by how many percent a value has increased or decreased, dividing by the original value

name: Percentage point
description: Percentage point: the difference between two percentages, so going from 20 % to 25 % is a rise of 5 percentage points.

name: Explain the difference between percent and percentage points
description: explain why a rise from 20 % to 25 % is 5 percentage points but 25 percent, and use each term correctly

name: Growth factor
description: Growth factor: the number the original value is multiplied by to give the new value, 1 + p/100 for an increase of p % and 1 − p/100 for a decrease.

name: Calculate the growth factor from a percentage
description: find the growth factor from a percentage increase or decrease, and the percentage from a growth factor

name: Calculate a new value with a growth factor
description: calculate the new value after a percentage change by multiplying by the growth factor

name: Find the original value from the new value
description: find the value before a percentage change by dividing the new value by the growth factor

name: Calculate the total effect of several percentage changes
description: calculate the total change after several different percentage changes by multiplying their growth factors, and explain why the percentages cannot simply be added

name: Calculate repeated percentage change with a power
description: calculate the value after the same percentage change repeated n times, as the original value times the growth factor to the power n

name: Model a percentage change over time with a digital tool
description: model a practical situation with repeated percentage change in a spreadsheet or GeoGebra, and read answers from the table or graph

name: Find when a growing amount reaches a given value
description: find how many periods it takes for a value that changes by a fixed percentage to reach a given amount, with a spreadsheet or by solving an equation in GeoGebra

name: Gross and net income
description:
Gross income: income before tax is deducted.
Net income: what is paid out after tax and other deductions.

name: Calculate net income
description: calculate net income from gross income, tax percentage and other deductions

name: Price index
description: Price index: a number showing the price level in one year compared with a base year, whose index is set to 100.

name: Calculate with a price index
description: use that price divided by index is the same in two years to find a price, an index or the price change between years

name: Krone value
description: Krone value: how much one krone buys compared with the base year, found as 100 divided by the price index.

name: Calculate the krone value
description: calculate the krone value from a price index, and say what it means that it has fallen

name: Nominal wage and real wage
description:
Nominal wage: the wage in kroner as it is paid out.
Real wage: the wage adjusted for price changes, showing what it can actually buy.

name: Calculate real wage
description: calculate real wage from nominal wage and price index, and decide whether purchasing power has risen or fallen

name: Explain how price index, krone value and real wage are connected
description: explain how a change in the price index affects krone value and real wage, using an example with numbers

name: Set up a budget in a spreadsheet
description: set up a monthly budget in a spreadsheet with formulas for totals and balance, and adjust it when income or expenses change

name: Interest rate
description: Interest rate: the price of borrowing, or the reward for saving, given as a percentage of the amount per period.

name: Annuity loan and serial loan
description:
Annuity loan: a loan where every payment is the same, so the share that is interest falls over time.
Serial loan: a loan where the instalment is the same each time, so the payment falls over time.

name: Effective interest rate
description: Effective interest rate: the total yearly cost of a loan, including fees, as a percentage of the amount borrowed.

name: Calculate the cost of a loan with a spreadsheet
description: set up a repayment plan for an annuity loan and a serial loan in a spreadsheet, and find the total cost of each

name: Calculate how credit card debt grows
description: calculate how an unpaid credit card debt grows over time with its interest rate and fees

name: Assess a choice about borrowing
description: assess a choice between loans, credit card and saving using calculations, and argue for the consequences for personal finances

name: Categorical and numerical data
description:
Categorical data: observations that are categories, such as favourite sport.
Numerical data: observations that are numbers, such as height.

name: Frequency, relative frequency and cumulative frequency
description:
Frequency: how many times a value occurs.
Relative frequency: the frequency as a share of all observations, often in percent.
Cumulative frequency: the sum of the frequencies up to and including a value.

name: Make a frequency table
description: make a table with frequency, relative frequency and cumulative frequency from a data set

name: Class interval and class midpoint
description:
Class interval: a range of values that observations are grouped into.
Class midpoint: the value halfway between the limits of a class interval.

name: Present data in a suitable diagram
description: choose a diagram that suits the data, such as a bar chart, pie chart, line chart or histogram, and draw it clearly labelled

name: Mean, median and mode
description:
Mean: the sum of the observations divided by how many there are.
Median: the middle value when the observations are sorted.
Mode: the value that occurs most often.

name: Calculate mean, median and mode
description: calculate mean, median and mode from a list of values or a frequency table

name: Estimate the mean from grouped data
description: estimate the mean of grouped data using class midpoints

name: Range and interquartile range
description:
Range: the largest value minus the smallest.
Interquartile range: the upper quartile minus the lower quartile, the spread of the middle half of the data.

name: Calculate range and interquartile range
description: find the range, the quartiles and the interquartile range of a data set

name: Standard deviation
description: Standard deviation: a measure of how far the observations typically lie from the mean.

name: Find the standard deviation with a digital tool
description: find the standard deviation of a data set with a spreadsheet or GeoGebra, and say what it tells about the data

name: Choose suitable measures of centre and spread
description: choose which measure of centre and which measure of spread best describe a data set, for example when there are extreme values, and justify the choice

name: Analyse and present findings from a data set
description: analyse a real data set from the local community or the media with diagrams and measures, and present what it shows in words

name: Judge whether a statistical presentation is misleading
description: judge whether a diagram or a claim with numbers in the media gives a fair picture, for example a cut axis or percent confused with percentage points

name: Perimeter, area and volume
description:
Perimeter: the length around a figure.
Area: how much surface a figure covers, measured in square units.
Volume: how much space a solid takes up, measured in cubic units.

name: Convert between units of length, area and volume
description: convert between units such as mm, cm, m and km, their square and cubic units, and litres

name: Calculate perimeter and area of plane figures
description: calculate perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapeziums, circles and composite figures

name: Calculate the volume and surface area of solids
description: calculate the volume and surface area of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres

name: Pythagoras' theorem
description: Pythagoras' theorem: in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

name: Use Pythagoras' theorem to find a side
description: find a missing side in a right-angled triangle, and decide whether a triangle is right-angled

name: Similar figures
description: Similar figures: figures with the same shape, where corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

name: Decide whether two triangles are similar
description: decide whether two triangles are similar, and justify it with angles or side ratios

name: Calculate unknown sides in similar figures
description: calculate unknown sides in similar figures by setting up equal ratios

name: Scale
description: Scale: the ratio between a length on a drawing or map and the same length in reality, as in 1 : 50 000.

name: Calculate with a scale
description: calculate real lengths from a map or drawing and drawing lengths from real ones, and find the scale from a pair of lengths

name: Use geometry in a practical task
description: plan a practical task such as painting a room or measuring a height with similar triangles, calculate the lengths, areas, volumes and amounts needed, and allow for waste as a percentage

name: Write formulas in a spreadsheet
description: write formulas in a spreadsheet that refer to other cells, copy them down a column, and add up columns
